legend: For an arbitrary grid, Robot defines its beauty to be the sum of elements in the grid.

Robot gives you an array a%%ZSMJ0%% of length n%%ZSMJ1%% and an array b%%ZSMJ2%% of length m%%ZSMJ3%%. You construct a n%%ZSMJ4%% by m%%ZSMJ5%% grid M%%ZSMJ6%% such that Mi,j=ai⋅bj%%ZSMJ7%% for all 1≤i≤n%%ZSMJ8%% and 1≤j≤m%%ZSMJ9%%.

Then, Robot gives you q%%ZSMJ10%% queries, each consisting of a single integer x%%ZSMJ11%%. For each query, determine whether or not it is possible to perform the following operation exactly once so that M%%ZSMJ12%% has a beauty of x%%ZSMJ13%%:
Choose integers r%%ZSMJ14%% and c%%ZSMJ15%% such that 1≤r≤n%%ZSMJ16%% and 1≤c≤m%%ZSMJ17%%
Set Mi,j%%ZSMJ18%% to be 0%%ZSMJ19%% for all ordered pairs (i,j)%%ZSMJ20%% such that i=r%%ZSMJ21%%, j=c%%ZSMJ22%%, or both.

Note that queries are not persistent, meaning that you do not actually set any elements to 0%%ZSMJ23%% in the process — you are only required to output if it is possible to find r%%ZSMJ24%% and c%%ZSMJ25%% such that if the above operation is performed, the beauty of the grid will be x%%ZSMJ26%%. Also, note that you must perform the operation for each query, even if the beauty of the original grid is already x%%ZSMJ27%%.
input: The first line contains three integers n%%ZSMJ28%%, m%%ZSMJ29%%, and q%%ZSMJ30%% (1≤n,m≤2⋅105,1≤q≤5⋅104%%ZSMJ31%%) — the length of a%%ZSMJ32%%, the length of b%%ZSMJ33%%, and the number of queries respectively.
The second line contains n%%ZSMJ34%% integers a1,a2,…,an%%ZSMJ35%% (0≤|ai|≤n%%ZSMJ36%%).
The third line contains m%%ZSMJ37%% integers b1,b2,…,bm%%ZSMJ38%% (0≤|bi|≤m%%ZSMJ39%%).

The following q%%ZSMJ40%% lines each contain a single integer x%%ZSMJ41%% (1≤|x|≤2⋅105%%ZSMJ42%%), the beauty of the grid you wish to achieve by setting all elements in a row and a column to 0%%ZSMJ43%%.
output: For each testcase, output "YES" (without quotes) if there is a way to perform the aforementioned operation such that the beauty is x%%ZSMJ44%%, and "NO" (without quotes) otherwise.
You can output "YES" and "NO" in any case (for example, strings "yES", "yes" and "Yes" will be recognized as a positive response).

In the second query, selecting r=3%%ZSMJ48%% and c=5%%ZSMJ49%% creates a grid with beauty −3%%ZSMJ50%%.
In the third query, selecting r=3%%ZSMJ51%% and c=3%%ZSMJ52%% creates a grid with beauty 5%%ZSMJ53%%.
